audit.whatIsWrong: Chart gave Singed levels 2 and 3 and 'Skill' at 1 and 6, while the page's own prose says 'Quinn owns levels 1 through 3 cleanly', 'The lane is simply hers here', and 'she still controls the pacing of this lane at level 6'.
audit.why: Quinn out-ranges Singed at 1025 on Blinding Assault with a Harrier proc on every first hit, and Vault resets her spacing on 12s. Singed has no answer until Rylai's. The packet chart also reads Quinn at 1, 2, 3 and 6.
audit.corrected: Chart flipped as one group: win[0], win[1], win[2], win[4] to Quinn plus the matching phases sides. Levels 4-5 stay Skill (whys[3] calls it a genuine skill matchup) and both item stages stay Singed.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown numbers anywhere; breakdown.cooldowns was template filler.
audit.why: Blinding Assault is 11/10.5/10/9.5/9s at 1025 range, Vault 12/11/10/9/8s at 675, Heightened Senses 50s at rank 1. Vault's 12s at rank 1 is the whole matchup: it is the only thing that resets her spacing, and while it is down she is standing in poison with nothing to escape on.
audit.corrected: Rank-1 numbers and ranges written into breakdown.cooldowns and phases[1].why.

audit.whatIsWrong: Five strings claim Blinding Assault blinds Singed and thereby stops him casting Fling.
audit.why: Riot's own text: 'Quinn calls Valor to mark an enemy and hinder its vision before damaging all enemies in the immediate area.' It hinders vision, it does not disarm abilities. Fling is a 125-range targeted cast on a unit you are standing next to. The page was teaching players to hold their strongest ability for a reason that does not exist. whys[1] also calls it a 'blind-and-slow' — there is no slow on it either; the kit flags only 'zone'.
audit.corrected: All five restated: her Q shortens your sight range and pokes, it does not stop Fling.

audit.whatIsWrong: Mega Adhesive's grounding was never connected to Vault, and Behind Enemy Lines being cancellable was absent entirely.
audit.why: Vault carries the dash flag, 'mobility that grounding and walls can deny', and Mega Adhesive grounds. Glue on her feet means Vault does not fire at all — stronger and simpler than the page's version, where she vaults and is then rooted on landing. Behind Enemy Lines is flagged channel, 'interruptible — any CC cancels it', so Fling ends her roam takeoff.
audit.corrected: Written into late, wants.you[1], dosFull[2], dontsFull[1] and breakdown.cooldowns.

edits.before: Quinn owns levels 1 through 3 cleanly — Harrier passive marks you for bonus damage every few seconds and her Q blind shuts down your ability to run at her safely, because a blinded Singed can't Fling accurately and walks into free poke. Don't try to trade at all; you are not a level-1 champion. Set up the proxy pattern immediately: position between her tower and the wave so Poison Trail drains minions while she has to decide whether to stop you or farm. Accept that she will win every direct exchange in this window and focus entirely on accelerating your gold lead through denial rather than damage.
edits.after: Quinn owns levels 1 through 3 cleanly — Harrier marks you for bonus damage every few seconds and Blinding Assault chips you from 1025 while hindering your vision, so you eat poke for nothing every time you step up. Don't try to trade at all; you are not a level-1 champion. Set up the proxy pattern immediately: position between her tower and the wave so Poison Trail drains minions while she has to decide whether to stop you or farm. Accept that she will win every direct exchange in this window and focus entirely on accelerating your gold lead through denial rather than damage.

edits.before: Once Rylai's Crystal Scepter completes, this lane flips entirely in your favour. Quinn can no longer walk out of Poison Trail and her Vault knockback becomes a liability: if she uses it to escape while standing inside your Mega Adhesive, the root procs and she is stuck in a slowing cloud until she dies. Two items in you are an almost uncatchable split-push engine she genuinely cannot 1v1, and her roam threat is neutralised by the fact that you threaten the turret every time she leaves. Force her to stay — then take the tower when she doesn't.
edits.after: Once Rylai's Crystal Scepter completes, this lane flips entirely in your favour. Quinn can no longer walk out of Poison Trail, and Mega Adhesive is the answer to Vault: the glue grounds it, so the dash never fires and she is stuck in a slowing cloud until she dies. Two items in you are an almost uncatchable split-push engine she genuinely cannot 1v1, and her roam threat is neutralised because Behind Enemy Lines is a channel your Fling cancels. Force her to stay — then take the tower when she leaves.
